Matrix multiplication is defined when the number of columns in the first matrix equals the number of rows in the second matrix.

Matrix A is 2 × 7 (2 rows, 7 columns).
Matrix B is 7 × 5 (7 rows, 5 columns).

Since the number of columns in A (7) equals the number of rows in B (7), the product AB is defined.

The resulting matrix will have dimensions equal to the number of rows of A and the number of columns of B, which is 2 × 5.

Answer: B
